messages:
maria (Product): Hey team, putting up the draft PRD/RFC for smart routing + fallback policies. Link: https://confluence/redwood/smart-routing-draft (please review). Key asks: 1) clear tier-to-region mapping, 2) compatible model variant rules for fallback, 3) launch acceptance criteria and rollout plan. TL;DR attached below.

kevin (Eng Platform): Skimming now. Can we make the policy format as small, composable rules so the router can evaluate cheaply? e.g. priority, latency_slo, fallbacks list.

david (Eng Runtime): Agreed with kevin. Also note that runtime needs a fast compatibility check — ideally precomputed compatibility matrix (modelA -> modelA-quant, modelA -> modelB-small). Can't do heavy checks on request path.

maria (Product): Good point. Draft acceptance criteria (please comment):
- Router serves >=99.95% of requests with primary tier within SLA in canary region.
- When primary model unavailable, fallback latency delta <= +50ms median vs primary for 90% of traffic.
- Fallbacks must preserve semantic parity: automated evaluation on 3 customer prompt-sets shows <=3% regression in top-1 quality metric.
- Admin-visible audit trail for every routed fallback (model, reason, region).

olivia (SRE): SLOs look ok but +50ms may be optimistic for cross-region fallback. Add metrics to track: fallback_count, fallback_latency_delta_p50/p95, fallback_error_rate. We need rate-based throttles so fallback storms don't cascade.

raj (Security): Two items: 1) For private/VPC deployments, routing decisions must not leak region metadata to hosted control plane logs unless customer opts in. 2) Enforce model variant allowlists per tenant (can't fallback to unapproved 3rd-party models).

emma (Solutions): From customer asks: fintech customers want tier-mapped routing: 'compliance' tier -> on-prem primary, hosted fallback only if customer whitelist allows. Also need sticky routing by session to avoid inconsistency mid-conversation.

kevin (Eng Platform): Implementation note: propose policy schema (yaml/json) like:
```json
{
  "id": "policy-123",
  "priority": 10,
  "match": {"tenant_tier": "gold", "region": "eu-west-1"},
  "primary": {"model": "redwood-7b", "deployment": "dedicated-eu"},
  "fallbacks": [
    {"model": "redwood-7b-quant", "reason": "capacity", "compatibility": "kv-cache-compatible"},
    {"model": "redwood-3b", "reason": "region-failover", "compatibility": "approximate"}
  ],
  "route_policies": {"max_fallback_rate": 0.05, "sticky_session_seconds": 3600}
}
```
This keeps evaluation fast.

david (Eng Runtime): Need to define compatibility labels: exact, kv-cache-compatible, approximate (semantic fallbacks). Runtime will consult precomputed compatibility table and short-circuit if label is missing.

maria (Product): Edge cases we should cover in PRD:
- Partial model degradation (slow but still returning) -> should we prefer local capacity throttling vs fallback?
- Token-limit mismatch (primary supports longer context than fallback). Must signal to caller and avoid silent truncation.
- Cross-tenant failovers: avoid using a fallback model that has data residency implications.

olivia (SRE): For rollout:
- Stage 1: internal canary (10% traffic, single region) for 48h. Monitor fallback metrics.
- Stage 2: opt-in customers + staging tenants for 1 week.
- Stage 3: broad rollout with automatic rollback on safety triggers (fallback_error_rate > 1% or quality regression > 5%).
Also add a canary override flag to disable fallback per-tenant quickly.

raj (Security): Add acceptance criteria: tenant allowlist enforced, KMS keys not exposed in logs, audit logs retained for X days (configurable).

emma (Solutions): Can we add a user-visible explanation for fallbacks in console: "Requests routed to fallback due to capacity" + per-request link to audit. Customers ask for this.

kevin (Eng Platform): Ops stuff: need a compact metrics payload from router to console: {model_primary, model_served, reason, latency_ms, tenant, region}. This can be batched.

maria (Product): Next steps: I'll update doc with schema and acceptance criteria by EOD. Please add inline comments on confluence. If no major objections, I'll spin up RFC PR and tag @eng-runtime and @sre for signoff.

infra-bot: RFC #382 created: https://github.com/redwood/infrastructure/pulls/382 (maria/smart-routing)

kevin (Eng Platform): Quick question — how do we want to handle version pinning? Should policies reference model version hashes or human names? I vote hashes with friendly alias.

david (Eng Runtime): Hash + alias. Runtime resolves alias to pinned hash at deploy time; fallback can be to alias with defined compatibility guarantees.

maria (Product): Great. Thanks all — leaving these open for comments. If you can thumbs up the RFC when you approve that will help prioritization :thumbsup:
